facts.statement: Aethaspis was an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Devonian period.
facts.quote: Aethaspis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish from the Devonian period.

facts.statement: The genus Aethaspis was described by Denison in 1958.
Aethaspis belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Aethaspis is classified within the class Placodermi.
Aethaspis lived from the Lochkovian to the Emsian stages, between 419.62 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Emsian (419.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: Two species were described by Denison in 1958: Aethaspis major, which is the type species, and Aethaspis utahensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: Aethaspis major Denison, 1958 (type) Aethaspis utahensis Denison, 1958
